text:
sanjay: heads-up — main CI went red right after my docs-only PR merged (PR #4321). job `deploy-helm` failed in post-merge step. Anyone awake to eyeball? :wave:
ci-bot: [AUTOMATION] build 12345 — job `deploy-helm` FAILED (exit code 1). Short log:
```
Error: UPGRADE FAILED: rendered manifests contain a resource that already exists. Unable to continue with release: rolebindings.rbac.authorization.k8s.io \"redwood-inference:release-service\" already exists
```
maria: hmm interesting, docs-only shouldn't touch charts. did your PR include a changelog script or release job change?
sanjay: only updated README and release notes script path; i did not touch infra. i did rename a folder (`docs/helm -> docs/charts`) but no chart files. :thinking_face:
alex: can someone run `helm template` against that chart? maybe a previous release left a dangling resource with the same name and our post-merge deploy tries to create it again.
tess: oncall, any chance this is due to the new SA clusterrole change we rolled out yesterday? we renamed a role binding prefix.
oncall: i saw a handful of flakes earlier but not this. i'll pull the failing job logs and run a rerun now. can whoever has quick repro steps paste them? :eyes:
sanjay: thanks — yiou can rerun with `./cictl rerun --job deploy-helm --build 12345`
ci-bot: rerun queued by oncall (build 12346).
oncall: rerun started. attaching the full `kubectl get rolebindings -A | grep release-service` output in a sec.
ci-bot: rerun finished — job `deploy-helm` FAILED again (build 12346). same error.
maria: ok two consistent failures — likely a chart release name collision or our deploy now tries to create cluster-scoped resources it shouldn't. sanjay, did your changelog rename affect the release name template? check `chart/Chart.yaml` and release name interpolation.
sanjay: i'm checking. my PR touched docs only, but the release pipeline reads the repo path to set release name. i added a `docs/charts` dir so the heuristics might have picked up the wrong path. that's plausible.
alex: quick triage plan: 1) check what release name the pipeline used (`helm get` against the cluster or `helm list --all-namespaces`), 2) if it tried to create a cluster rolebinding, revert or patch pipeline to skip cluster RB creation for docs deploys, 3) if urgent, revert the merge to unblock.
oncall: i ran `helm list --all-namespaces | grep release-service` — it exists in `kube-system` from previous manual testing. looks like new deploy attempted to create same name in `redwood-system` and failed.
tess: got it. that explains the error. we should either rename the release in the pipeline or delete the stale one. removing cluster-scoped resources needs prod approval — not ideal for fast fix.
maria: revert seems fastest. can someone open a revert PR referencing this thread and ping release team? i'll coordinate approvals.
sanjay: i can open revert now. quick question — will revert break anything else? it only reverts the docs rename commit. should be safe.
oncall: please open revert and tag `@release` and `@security` for the cluster rolebinding risk. i'll hold on further reruns until we revert.
sanjay: done — PR #4322 created to revert the docs rename: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/4322 :shipit:
maria: approving rollback flow. @release can you expedite merge?
alex: once merged, oncall please trigger a rerun of `deploy-helm` and report back. if it still fails we'll bisect the pipeline.
oncall: acknowledged. rerun queued after revert merges. will post updates. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: [AUTOMATION] PR #4322 merged by merge-bot.
oncall: rerun kicked (build 12347).
ci-bot: build 12347 — job `deploy-helm` SUCCEEDED.
oncall: ok green now. root cause: pipeline picked up docs dir rename and formed a different release namespace/name, collided with existing cluster-scoped rolebinding. reverting rename prevents pipeline from trying to create the duplicate.
maria: filing a follow-up ticket to make release name detection explicit and not rely on path heuristics. CC: ops.
sanjay: thanks all for quick help — i'll include a note in the commit history and follow-up with the release team to harden heuristics. :relieved:
tess: nice catch. lesson: docs renames can have infra side effects. :facepalm:
alex: adding a small unit in CI to validate release name resolution would prevent this.
oncall: closing thread, will add postmortem blurb to the incident log.
